source.title: Begin Where You Are
source.theme: Starting honestly, rather than starting well.
source.purpose: Starting with one honest picture of the present can reduce the pressure to solve everything. Today helps you notice what needs attention, what you hope may become different, and what has already helped you keep going.
teaching: People postpone difficult things for many reasons: fear, exhaustion, uncertainty, limited support, present demands, or a response that has helped them cope. Delay is not proof of laziness or unwillingness.
Today offers a simple map: Where am I now? What needs attention? What do I hope may become a little different? What has helped me keep going?
You will not be asked to relive anything, explain yourself, or disclose private details. The purpose is orientation, not breakthrough.

selections.prompt: As you sit down with this, how is it being you today?
What brought you here — in plain words?
labels: I want to feel more hope or possibility

oneHonestStep.prompt: What small step feels genuinely possible before tomorrow?

practice.title: Reflection Practice — one honest “Right now…”
practice.summary: A short way of telling yourself the truth without having to explain or justify it to anyone.
steps: Begin outwardly. Notice three neutral things around you—objects, colours, shapes or sounds.
Choose one broad area from what brought you here. No event, person or history needs to be named.

You could write on paper, in a notebook or in a note on your phone: ‘Right now, this part of life feels…’ Then finish that sentence in your own words. You can instead say the opening and finish it privately aloud, or consider it silently. One plain phrase is enough.
If it feels workable, write or say: ‘What I wish could be a little different is…’ Then finish that sentence in your own words. ‘I do not know yet’ is a complete ending.
Name one resource that has helped you reach today—a quality in you, a person, a practice, faith, practical help or simple necessity.
Finish with: ‘I can begin here without solving this today,’ and return your attention to the room.
practice.notRequired: Gentler route: choose only one sentence opening. Read-only route: read the openings without answering. No writing, disclosure, decision or action is required.

reviewChecks: Do not attribute steadiness to the app or claim recovery.
